sources.entry: django-cors-headers - Handles Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) headers for Django apps.

summary.one_liner: A Django app that adds Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) headers to responses so in-browser requests from other origins can reach a Django application.
summary.what_it_does: Installs as a Django app plus a middleware class (CorsMiddleware) that adds CORS response headers. Allowed origins can be set as an explicit list, as regular expressions, or as allow-all, and URL paths can be limited with a regex such as one covering only /api/. Settings control allowed HTTP methods and request headers, exposed headers, preflight max age, credentials (cookies), and Private Network Access headers. The README also covers CSRF integration via CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS and a check_request_enabled signal that lets custom code decide per request whether to allow CORS, for example by looking up origins in a database model.
use_cases: let a separate frontend app call a Django API from the browser
restrict cross-origin access to specific domains or subdomains
allow cross-origin requests only to /api/ URLs
allow cookies in cross-site requests with CORS_ALLOW_CREDENTIALS
decide CORS access per request from a database of allowed sites
combine CSRF trusted origins with CORS for cross-site forms
how_to_run: Add "corsheaders.middleware.CorsMiddleware" near the top of MIDDLEWARE, before CommonMiddleware
Set at least one of CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS, CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGIN_REGEXES, or CORS_ALLOW_ALL_ORIGINS in Django settings
notable: Settings-driven: allowed origins as list, regex, or allow-all, with legacy alias names still supported
Optional signal hook (check_request_enabled) for custom per-request allow logic
Can restrict CORS to URL patterns via CORS_URLS_REGEX
Documents CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS interaction, since CORS and CSRF are separate
Maintained since 2016 after earlier unmaintained period, per the About section
caveats: CORS_ALLOW_ALL_ORIGINS=True lets any website make cross-origin requests, which the README calls dangerous
CorsMiddleware must be placed high in MIDDLEWARE or other middleware may generate responses without CORS headers
Session cookies are SameSite=Lax by default, so cross-site cookie use needs SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE changed to 'None'
